name: Le Méridien Tampa, The Courthouse
insider_take: This isn't just any hotel—you're sleeping in Tampa's former federal courthouse where Al Capone was once tried for tax evasion in 1931.
whats_special: The stunning Art Deco architecture dates back to 1905, featuring original terrazzo floors, soaring 20-foot ceilings, and restored courtrooms now transformed into elegant event spaces. The building's iconic clock tower remains a downtown Tampa landmark, while the hotel seamlessly blends historic grandeur with modern Le Méridien sophistication.
pro_tip: Book a room on the upper floors for panoramic views of Tampa Bay and the Hillsborough River, and don't miss cocktails at the rooftop bar housed in the original judge's chambers.
dont_miss: Explore the Tampa Riverwalk just steps away, catch a Lightning game at nearby Amalie Arena, or take the historic streetcar to Ybor City's vibrant nightlife scene. The hotel's location puts you within walking distance of the Tampa Theatre, a stunning 1926 atmospheric movie palace.
pros: Historic courthouse architecture with modern luxury amenities
Prime downtown Tampa location near cultural attractions
Sophisticated rooftop bar with city skyline views
Boutique hotel experience with personalized service
cons: Limited parking options in downtown location
Historic building may have smaller room sizes
